thread:
maya: Heads-up — infra-ci flagged a perf regression when we switched to per-channel FP8 kernels with the new calibration set. can folks share quick takes on dataset curation?

juan: saw the alert. numbers?

infra-ci-bot: Regression detected: serving-p90 latency +18% on short seqs (<=32 tokens) after roll-forward. Run: canary-2026-03-09.

maya: thanks. quick summary from profiling: kernel selection time increased due to per-channel scale tables being computed/loaded at kernel launch for ~30% of layers; KV warmup hit increases token processing jitter. overall throughput down on small-batch workloads.

sasha: hmm. per-channel quant usually gives better quality but the extra metadata per layer can blow up kernel setup for small sequences. did we prepack scales into the compiled kernel?

juan: we didn't for this roll — we were still using runtime compute of scales bc dataset varied (different ranges). that avoids recompile but costs startup.

owen: alternative: two-phase calibration dataset. a small stratified pass to estimate scale distributions, then generate a compact "packable" calibration summary for fast startup. e.g., compute per-layer mean/std and 2 percentile bounds, then embed into kernel header.

liam: +1. also think we should trim outliers before the final pass. a few extreme tokens from long-tail prompts drove scale to huge values and forced big dynamic ranges. trimming 0.5% tails reduced the number of layers switching to FP32 fallback.

maya: curious — how did you pick trim threshold? any objective metric?

liam: used an empirical approach: run per-layer maxabs distribution, then cut anything above the 99.5th percentile, recompute scales and evaluate on eval-set. trade-off: slight BLEU/ROUGE hit in edge cases but big perf wins.

sasha: we should be careful: per-tensor (per-row) quant was much cheaper runtime wise but accuracy drop on attention heads was notable for certain models. For redwood-3b, per-channel preserves head-wise behavior. Maybe hybrid: per-channel for attention and per-tensor for FFN?

juan: that matches some kernel experiments. FFN MatMuls tolerate per-tensor more. attention uses low-rank structure that per-channel captures. but hybrid increases codec complexity — kernel selection logic needs to be aware of layer type.

diane: ops-level routing is okay if we keep deterministic fallback. propose config knobs: calibrate_mode: [fast, balanced, strict]; fast -> per-tensor + aggressive trimming, balanced -> hybrid with 99th pct trim, strict -> per-channel no trim. these are user-facing presets and behind the scenes map to kernels and packing policies.

maya: nice. question for ML folks: does two-pass stratified sampling + outlier-trim change eval regression likelihood? we need to avoid quality regressions in customer traffic.

liam: in our small experiments, two-pass with 2k stratified + 512 focused outlier samples gave stable metrics vs full 10k set for >95% of eval prompts. the outliers that changed tended to be long-context system prompts that we can flag separately and route to fallback model.

owen: routing is important — we can add a policy: if input length>1024 or contains flagged tokens -> bypass quantized fast path and use full-precision fallback. that keeps tail quality.

juan: what's the plan for KV cache? the bigger problem was KV warmup interacting with kernel start-up. if we can precompute and embed scales and pack weights during model load (not at first request), KV warmup won't pay the kernel-selection tax per request. trade is higher memory on load and longer cold-start.

maya: agreed. for Dedicated customers we can favor eager pack-on-load. for hosted free tier maybe lazy but cache the packed kernels in-memory across requests.

sasha: small note — prepack increases model load RAM by ~6% in our FP8-per-channel experiments, and decreases p90 by ~22% on short seqs. numbers look worth it for most production cases.

diane: should we add an infra experiment? A/B: current rollout vs pack-on-load + hybrid quant + 99pct trim. monitor latency, throughput, and a prompt-quality eval set.

maya: yes — let's run A/B for 48h on low-traffic shard. juan can you own the experiment?

juan: I’ll spin it up. timeline: config and kernel-pack code today, canary tomorrow morning, collect 48h. I’ll post perf diffs and eval deltas.

liam: I’ll prepare the stratified sampling script and the tiny eval harness (2k stratified + 512 outlier checks).

nowen: I can add the routing rule for >1024 length so we don't accidentally degrade long-context customers during the test.

maya: perfect. small follow-ups: add telemetry for "kernel_pack_state" and "quant_mode_per_layer" so we can slice metrics by layer type. and add a flag to force-per-tensor for debugging.

juan: noted. infra-ci-bot will post canary status.

infra-ci-bot: Canary scheduled: shard canary-quant-2026-03-10-08. Monitoring: latency, error-rate, quant-quality.

maya: thanks everyone. will reconvene after 48h. :thumbsup:
